characters: Kwabena: a fourteen-year-old JHS 3 student wearing safety goggles and a workshop apron, holding a steel rule and try-square.
Efua: his classmate holding a 1 : 10 orthographic scale drawing on graph paper with a compass and ruler.
Asana: their classmate testing computer-desk posture and screen height in the ICT lab.
Mr Mensah-Bonsu: the Career Technology woodwork and technical-drawing teacher.

notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.

teacherGuide.overview: Connects abstract BECE geometry (Pythagoras’ theorem, scale ratios, surface area) directly to Career Technology structural triangulation, timber seasoning, precision marking-out tools, and Computing workstation ergonomics.
learningGoals: Explain why triangulated frames resist deformation and why timber is seasoned.
Use Pythagoras’ theorem (a² + b² = c²) and 1 : 10 scale ratios to calculate structural braces.
Select correct workshop marking-out tools and demonstrate healthy ICT workstation ergonomics.

beforeReading: Build a quick 4-stick pin-jointed square and a 3-stick triangle using paper strips and split pins—let students push both!
whileReading: Pause on Page 3 to verify why 60² + 80² = 10,000 gives a 100 cm brace—and why adding 60 + 80 = 140 cm would never fit.
afterReading: Audit your school ICT chairs/desks for ergonomic angles and draw a 1 : 10 scale elevation of one desk bay with a diagonal brace.
discussion: Where can you spot triangulation right now in pylon towers, Adomi Bridge trusses, bicycle frames, or market roof rafters?
reflection: How does "measure twice, cut once" save money, timber, and time in engineering?

mathsExtension.task: On a 1 : 20 technical drawing, a wooden workbench top measures 9 cm long by 3.5 cm wide. Find its actual length and width in metres, and calculate its real top surface area in m².
mathsExtension.answer: Actual length = 9 cm × 20 = 180 cm = 1.8 m. Actual width = 3.5 cm × 20 = 70 cm = 0.7 m. Area = 1.8 m × 0.7 m = 1.26 m².

support: Provide pre-cut 3-4-5 right-angled triangle card templates so learners verify a² + b² = c² visually by counting grid squares.
stretch: Distinguish between struts (members resisting compression) and ties (members resisting tension) inside a loaded roof truss.
